Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goal: Improve your search relevance by adding a lightweight reranker on top of existing lexical candidates. Expected win: +10-30% relevance lift on user queries depending on dataset.
- Scope for initial eval: ingest ~100k candidate pairs, run offline eval (MRR / Recall@k), then a short staged deployment for live metrics.
- Integration points we discussed: SDK setup, auth (service token), routing/canary, structured scoring outputs for downstream UI, and metric logging for offline evals.

Next steps:

Thanks Marissa — the plan looks good. A few clarifying technical questions from our side so we can scope engineering time: 

1) SDK / auth: Do you have an official Python SDK for the ranking endpoint? How do we handle service-to-service auth for our backend (short-lived tokens vs. API key)?
2) Endpoints & routing: Is there a dedicated /rank or /rerank endpoint? Can we route traffic to a canary model variant (low % of traffic) while keeping existing lexical pipeline in front?
3) Output format: We need structured scores per candidate (score, label, metadata) that map cleanly into our UI. Any constraints on payload size / response schema?
4) Candidate size / top_k: We typically send 50 candidates; how does top_k and candidate pruning affect latency and cost? Any guidelines for tuning top_k and candidate selection?
5) Metrics / logging: For offline eval, we’ll compute MRR, Recall@k, and NDCG. Does Redwood provide hooks or exportable logs (per-request scores, embeddings) to run these offline?
6) A question on ensembling: If we want to combine embeddings-based reranking with a transformer reranker, is that supported in the pipeline?

If you can send answers (or point us to docs), we can lock down a PoC timeline. Also cc’ing Priya (PM) who’ll be coordinating the PoC.

—Samir

Hi Samir — quick answers while Dev adds implementation details: 

- SDK: We have an official Python SDK that wraps the Ranking API and streaming generation. It’s pip-installable (package: redwood_inference). I’ll paste a minimal example in Dev’s note.
- Endpoint: /v1/rank is the dedicated ranking endpoint. You POST a JSON payload with candidates + context. Response contains an ordered list with scores.
- Canary routing: Supported. You can configure rollout/policies in the Console to only send X% traffic to the new reranker model.
- Ensembling: Supported via the pipeline config — you can run embedding similarity pre-filter then a transformer reranker, or average scores. We’ll recommend a staged approach (embeddings pre-filter -> reranker).

I’ll let Dev provide latency numbers and auth patterns.

—Alex
Senior Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@searchly.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@searchly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reranker integration — SDK/auth/ranking questions

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks for the clear list. Below are concrete answers and a recommended PoC plan. I’ve kept examples in Python and included recommended metrics and tuning steps.

1) SDK / auth
- SDK: pip install redwood_inference
- Minimal usage:
\  from redwood_inference import RankingClient
  client = RankingClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")  # supports API key or short-lived JWT
  response = client.rank(
      model="reranker-v1",
      context="user query text",
      candidates=[{"id": "c1", "text": "candidate A"}, {"id": "c2", "text": "candidate B"}],
      top_k=10
  )

- Auth patterns: We support static API keys for quick PoCs and short-lived JWTs (recommended) for production. JWTs integrate with your identity provider (OIDC) and can be minted by a small auth service. We also support mTLS for private deployments.

2) Endpoint & request/response
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rank
- Request payload (JSON): context, candidates (list of id/text/metadata), options (top_k, rerank_strategy).
- Response (JSON): ordered_candidates: [{"id":"c2","score":0.93,"features":{...}}, ...], all_candidates (optional), request_id, latency_ms.
- Payload limits: 1MB body for hosted API; recommended candidate text size < 4KB each to avoid token blow-up.

3) Routing / canary
- Console supports rollout policies per-model version. Configure canary at X% traffic or route by header (e.g., X-Test-Bucket). You can also set automatic fallback to a smaller/cheaper model if SLOs are breached.

4) Candidate size / top_k guidance
- Latency scales roughly linearly with number of candidates for transformer rerankers. For our reranker-v1 on an Nvidia A10g: median latency for 50 candidates ~ 120-180ms (batching and sequence length dependent).
- Cost: per-request cost proportional to tokens processed; embedding pre-filter reduces candidate count and cost. Typical pattern: use embedding similarity to get top 200 -> lexical filters to 50 -> reranker top_k=10/20.
- Tuning: start with top_k=10 for UI ranking; evaluate Recall@10 / MRR. If Recall@10 low, increase candidate pool or top_k. If latency too high, use a cheaper reranker or reduce top_k.

5) Metrics / logging for offline eval
- We emit request-level logs you can export: request_id, model_version, input_context, candidate_ids, returned_scores, latency_ms. Logs can be exported to your S3 or BigQuery (1:1 export) for offline metrics.
- For embeddings: we can export vector embeddings (checkpointed) for offline similarity experiments (subject to storage plan).
- Suggested offline metrics: MRR, Recall@k (k=5,10,20), NDCG@k, Precision@k, latency P50/P95.

6) Ensembling / pipeline patterns
- Supported: recommended pipeline is embeddings pre-filter (ANN) -> lexical prune -> transformer reranker. Alternatively, run both embedding-sim scores and reranker scores and blend (weighted sum) in the pipeline config. We can surface the intermediate scores in the response if you set options.return_all_scores=true.

7) Structured output and UI integration
- Response includes per-candidate metadata and score. Sample flattened response: 
  ordered_candidates: [{"id":"c2","score":0.93,"label":"answer","metadata":{"source":"kb/faq","doc_id":"123"}}, ...]
- This maps directly into your UI: use the score to order and metadata to display badges.

8) Practical PoC steps (1-2 week plan)
- Day 0-1: sample data export (you provide ~5-10k labeled queries with positive doc ids).
- Day 1-2: ingest candidates, run embedding pre-filter + reranker offline eval. We’ll share an eval report (MRR, Recall@k, NDCG) and recommended top_k.
- Day 3-5: short live canary (1-5% traffic) with metrics dashboard and request logs exported to your BigQuery.

9) Example eval query payload (POST /v1/rank):
{
  "context": "how do I reset my password",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"d_100","text":"To reset your password, go to settings...","metadata":{"source":"kb"}},
    {"id":"d_101","text":"Password can be reset from account page...","metadata":{"source":"forum"}}
  ],
  "options": {"top_k": 10, "return_all_scores": true}
}

10) Additional notes
- For offline MRR/NDCG computation we’ll provide a small notebook that consumes exported logs (we can push to your repo).
- If you want to try a low-cost quantized reranker for latency-sensitive paths, we can schedule a model variant.

If this looks good I can schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with Alex and an infra engineer to walk through the SDK and run a live demo against a small sample dataset.

Best,

Dev Patel
